headline: Chips Carry a Split Tape Into the New Week
body_html:
U.S. stocks closed the week on Friday, November 6, with a lopsided session. Semiconductors jumped 5.23% as a group, far ahead of everything else in our universe. Energy added 0.99% and materials 0.31%. Underneath, more stocks fell than rose: 236 advanced and 287 declined out of 525.

The leadership was concentrated in chips and the networking gear around them. Alpha and Omega Semiconductor gained 27.76%, Ubiquiti 15.29%, Extreme Networks 14.16%, Coherent 13.58% and Diodes 13.17%. Software slid 1.54%, consumer shares lost 1.63% and homebuilders gave up 2.10%. BlackLine tumbled 23.11% and eXp World Holdings dropped 20.72%. Healthcare was nearly flat at -0.15%, but individual moves were large: TransMedics rose 27.92% while Artivion and Natera fell 20.21% and 14.59%.

Looking to Monday, November 9, traders will weigh whether the chip rally can broaden. Headlines point to several themes to watch. Qatar says its mediation between Washington and Tehran continues, even after reports of missiles hitting Iran's Qeshm Island. The White House named Stephen Miller chief of staff after the midterm defeat. Kevin Hassett said the AI data-center build-out will go on regardless of the election result.

briefs.headline: Chip and networking names lead a narrow advance
briefs.body: Semiconductors rose 5.23% on Friday, the best showing of any group we track. Alpha and Omega Semiconductor gained 27.76%, and Coherent, Extreme Networks and Ubiquiti all rose more than 13%. The question for Monday is whether buyers extend beyond that corner of the market.

briefs.headline: Software, housing and consumer shares sag
briefs.body: Homebuilders lost 2.10%, consumer stocks 1.63% and software 1.54% on Friday. BlackLine fell 23.11%, eXp World Holdings 20.72% and Interface 18.72%. The weakness was sharp in individual names and left more decliners than gainers overall.

briefs.headline: Healthcare is flat on the surface, wild underneath
briefs.body: The healthcare group slipped just 0.15% on Friday, masking big single-stock swings. TransMedics jumped 27.92%, while Artivion dropped 20.21% and Natera fell 14.59%. Investors should expect stock-specific moves, not sector direction, to drive the group this week.

briefs.headline: Qatar says Iran mediation is still working
briefs.body: Qatar said its efforts to broker contact between the U.S. and Iran continue to hold back escalation. Iranian media reported two missiles striking Qeshm Island, and Washington sanctioned Canadian money-transfer firms over Iran-linked flows. Energy shares rose 0.99% Friday, and Monday's open may show how traders read the tension.

briefs.headline: Miller's promotion gives the White House a harder edge
briefs.body: President Trump elevated Stephen Miller to chief of staff following the midterm loss. Miller previously shaped the administration's immigration crackdown. Markets will watch for signs of how the shake-up affects the policy agenda, along with a House Oversight Democrat's warning to the president's family.

briefs.headline: Freight costs hand refiners an advantage
briefs.body: Surging shipping rates are helping U.S. refiners as discounts on crude widen, according to Reuters reporting. The shift supports the case for an energy group that gained 0.99% on Friday. Watch whether the freight and crude-spread trends persist into the new week.
